sources.headline: Photos: Crowds greet Pope Leo in Argentina after 40-year wait
sources.text: Pope Leo XIV urges Argentines to emulate their saints during his landmark visit, drawing crowds unseen for decades.Pope Leo XIV arrives to preside over Mass at the grounds of the Military Aviation School in Cordoba, Argentina. [Nicolas Aguilera/AP Photo]Published On 10 Nov 2026Pope Leo XIV has urged Argentinians to follow the “holy example” of the country’s saints and build a more “fraternal and caring nation”, as an estimated 650,000 people packed the central city of Cordoba for Mass.The 71-year-old pontiff, on a 12‑day Latin America tour less than a month after lung cancer surgery, on Tuesday celebrated the liturgy on the esplanade of a military aircraft factory.The Vatican said it was attended by 650,000 pilgrims, following Monday’s Mass in Buenos Aires, where about 2.5 million worshippers gathered – the largest of his pontificate so far.In Cordoba, Leo listed Argentinian saints and blessed figures as examples of a unity “between passion for the Gospel and commitment to building a fraternal and caring nation”, urging citizens to evangelise “at school and in the square, in the family and with friends, in the countryside and in the city, at the dairy farm and in the office”.Faithful travelled from across the country after nearly 40 years without a papal visit. “It was quite a journey,” said Erika Vinales, who travelled 2,000km (1,242 miles) from Patagonia with fellow teacher Elena Llanquenao.Throughout his three days in Argentina, Leo has repeatedly challenged President Javier Milei’s right-wing government to make the economy more inclusive, protect trade unions and reverse funding cuts that hurt the poor and people with disabilities.After nearly 40 years without a papal visit, faithful from the far north to Patagonia drove for hours and days to see the pontiff. [Nicolas Aguilera/AP Photo]Leo recalled Cordoba as a “land of saints”, home to some of Argentina’s most famous missionaries. [Andrew Medichini/AP Photo]“We are all called to holiness,” Leo said. “Today, it is our turn to follow the radiant example of holiness they have left with us.” [Gustavo Garello/AP Photo]Leo spoke of Argentina’s history of “reasons for gratitude and painful memories”, urging each generation to confront past injustices. [Gustavo Garello/AP Photo]The gathering reflected the broad appeal Leo has enjoyed in Argentina, extending beyond regular churchgoers. [Andrew Medichini/AP Photo]Throughout his three days in Argentina, Leo has repeatedly challenged President Javier Milei’s right-wing government to make the economy more inclusive, protect trade unions and reverse funding cuts that hurt the poor and people with disabilities. [Gustavo Garello/AP Photo]A worshipper holds her dog ahead of a Mass celebrated by Pope Leo XIV at the Military Aviation School in Cordoba, Argentina. [Nicolas Aguilera/AP Photo]The site for the liturgy was the grounds of the Argentine Aircraft Factory, a plant run by the air force for much of the 20th century that built the attack planes Argentina’s military first used in late 1975 to strike leftist rebels. [Andrew Medichini/AP Photo]Human rights groups estimate that about 30,000 people were killed or forcibly disappeared under Argentina’s 1976–1983 military dictatorship [Nicolas Aguilera/AP Photo]

sources.headline: In Argentina, Pope Leo Walks in the Giant Shadow of Francis
sources.text: Francis never returned to his home country after becoming pope, but the new pontiff will still be confronted with the overwhelming presence of his predecessor.

sources.headline: Pope Leo XIV draws huge crowds in Córdoba after record Buenos Aires mass
sources.text:
Pope Leo XIV urged Argentines on Tuesday to follow the holy example of the country’s best-known saints, as an estimated 650,000 people gathered in the central city of Córdoba for Mass.
The crowd came a day after an estimated 2.5 million people turned out to see the Pope in the Argentine capital, Buenos Aires, on Monday.
Faithful from all over Argentina drove for hours to attend the service, arriving from the far north of the country, from Patagonia in the south and from points in between.
Córdoba was chosen to host the Pope because of its central location. The city had gone nearly 40 years without a papal visit.
They include St. José Gabriel del Rosario Brochero, known as the “ Gaucho priest,” and “Mama Antula,” who in 2024 became Argentina’s first female saint. They were both canonised by the Argentine Pope Francis.
“We are all called to holiness,” he said. “These saints and blessed have already fulfilled their mission on Earth. Today, it is our turn to follow the radiant example of holiness they have left with us.”
After Mass, Leo surprised the crowds with a brief appearance on the balcony of the archbishop’s residence in downtown Córdoba, the same balcony from which St. John Paul II greeted Córdoba in 1987. Thousands of people chanting “León, León” packed the street below. “United, we can do anything,” the pope told them.
Erika Viñales, 39, and Elena Llanquenao, 54, religious education teachers from Santa Cruz province in Argentina’s Patagonia region, said they travelled 2,000 kilometres (more than 1,200 miles) to be on hand. “It was quite a journey,” Viñales said.
The mass in the city of Córdoba came ahead of a final mass in the town of Luján scheduled for Wednesday, the day on which the pope, also known as Robert Francis Prevost, will leave Argentina to travel to Peru.
Leo XIV posted on his X account: "My arrival in Argentina has, for me, a particular meaning: for twelve years, the universal Church listened to the voice of Pope Francis, who carried with him, in his memory and in his heart, the places, the people and the faith he received here."
"The truth is that to almost touch heaven with your hands is to be very close to it, to feel it in your own flesh," said Romeo Armando, a university student.
Meanwhile, Rosa Acevedo, a retired Argentine woman, could barely contain her emotion: "It is a very great feeling, something that fills me. I am going with all my heart full of blessings".
'Putting the person before the algorithm'
In Uruguay, a few days ago, the Pope warned at the Catholic University of Uruguay in Montevideo about the "dehumanisation" caused by AI: "It is urgent, then, that our school and university education contribute to the wise use of technologies and AI, putting the person before the algorithm and harmonising technical, emotional, social, spiritual and ecological intelligences".
Meanwhile, in Peru, the papal plane and its crew were blessed by Monsignor Paolo Rocco Gualtieri at Jorge Chávez International Airport in Lima on the eve of the pontiff's arrival.
A giant statue of Pope Leo XIV has been unveiled before his upcoming visit to the country in the port city of Callao, about 15 km from Lima. The Pope, who was born in the United States, holds Peruvian nationality and is returning to the country where he spent many years as a missionary and bishop.
